title: Income Tax Act 2025: Key Checks for Salaried Taxpayers in 2026
description: The new Income Tax Act, 2025, consolidates and updates existing tax laws for all taxpayers. Salaried individuals must meticulously review their payroll record.

faq.q: What is the Income Tax Act, 2025?
faq.a: The Income Tax Act, 2025, is a new, consolidated direct tax law that is expected to replace the existing Income Tax Act, 1961. It aims to simplify and modernise India's tax framework.

faq.q: How does it affect salaried individuals specifically?
faq.a: Salaried individuals will see changes in how their income is computed, new section references for deductions and exemptions, and revised reporting requirements in their ITR forms and Form 16.

faq.q: Will my tax-saving investments still be valid?
faq.a: While the underlying investments (like PPF, ELSS) are likely to remain, their tax treatment, applicable sections, or maximum deduction limits might be revised under the new Act. You must verify the updated provisions.

faq.q: When do these changes come into effect for my ITR?
faq.a: The provisions of the Income Tax Act, 2025, will apply to the financial year 2026-27 (starting April 1, 2026), meaning they will impact your Income Tax Return filed in Assessment Year 2027-28.

faq.q: Where can I find official information about the new Act?
faq.a: Official information, notifications, and FAQs will be published on the Income Tax Department's website and the Ministry of Finance's website.

faq.q: What if my employer does not update their payroll?
faq.a: If your employer fails to update their payroll system, your TDS deductions might be incorrect, leading to discrepancies in your Form 16 and potential issues during ITR filing. You should bring this to their attention promptly.

faq.q: Are NRIs also affected by the new Act?
faq.a: Yes, the Income Tax Act, 2025, will apply to all taxpayers, including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs), though specific provisions for NRIs might also be updated or modified.
